subject.title: refactor: remove expired plugin compatibility surfaces

question: Should the July 21, 2026 release intentionally remove plugin compatibility records whose registry windows do not expire until July 24–30, 2026?
rationale: The registry date is a published external-plugin contract, and only maintainers can choose whether to honor those dates, defer the removals, or delay the release.

options.title: Honor the recorded windows
options.body: Keep all records active until their individual removeAfter dates, then land the sweep after those dates.

options.title: Delay the release
options.body: Ship this sweep only in a release dated on or after July 30, 2026, preserving the selected removal set without shortening its announced windows.

options.title: Approve an early break
options.body: Explicitly accept the early external-plugin break and document a release exception with a supported migration and communication plan.

recommendation.title: Honor the recorded windows
recommendation.body: Keep all records active until their individual removeAfter dates, then land the sweep after those dates.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete authored the compatibility sweep and its current-head repair commits, making them the clearest available routing candidate for the release-contract decision.
